THE MOST BEGINNER-FRIENDLY WAYS TO LEARN

Learn by doing, in small steps

One idea, then a handful of exercises right away. Used by the Dutch Steps Method that takes learners from rules to about 2100.

In this app: Every unit is Learn, Practice, Apply.
Puzzles by theme, then mixed

Seeing the same pattern many times builds recognition. Mixing them teaches you to find the pattern yourself.

In this app: Train tab: one theme, or rated mixed puzzles.
Spaced repetition

Puzzles you miss come back after 1, 2, 4, 7 days until they stick. Later, the Woodpecker method repeats whole sets faster each time.

In this app: Review missed puzzles, on your daily plan.
Play slow, review every game

Slow games give you time to think. Reviewing them shows your real weaknesses.

In this app: Play tab with move grades and full review.
Endgames early

With few pieces you learn what each piece can do. Basic endings also win you half-points every month.

In this app: Endgame drills against Stockfish.
A coach who explains why

Feedback right after the move is how skills form fastest.

In this app: Every move graded and explained, with moves you can tap to see on the board.
